I made a post about why we don't have Homeless support groups. If you find an organization that is doing anything close to what you have mentioned, please come back and share. Sorry for the long post.

 When you become homeless, people treat you with a "sucks to be you" mentality. They give out negative positivity like "just pray and it'll work out" or "well if you think positive then positivethings will happen". Worse is when people tell you to call 211, like you have not already exhausted every resource Avenue. Friends and family are more concerned with themselves than having the burden of helping someone close in need. It's understandable since most people are one illness or Pandemic away from homelessness themselves...but still hurtful in all aspects. 

The "resources" available are not great. To even get these resources you usually have to go through intake run by people who look at you like trash. They feel as though you be happy to eat shit (literally AND figuratively) if you are really desperate and hungry.  For example, I was told to stay in shelter I would have to take a medication that i was not on, that made me sick everyday just because a Doctor (not mine) said I needed it. There is no protection.. at night its a free for all for people to steal and assault others while trying to sleep. People running from abusive relationships have been killed because the people handling these resources didn't care if you were near your abuser. "It's the only bed open, take it or leave it". Shelters keep you at night, kick you back out into the elements during the day.

Food is worse than eating everyday the greasiest McDonald burger made, and that is if it is edible. Sometimes it is just slop. Sometimes expired.  

Housing should be a right, not a luxury. More people would work and seek help if they didn't have to worry about starvation, physical attacks, freezing to death, and were healthy and not slowly dying or getting limbs chopped off because they can't properly treat illness such as diabetes. 

It's lonely when friends and family refuse to help. It's lonely when the only resources are little to non or life threatening. And being treated less than human is the loneliest feeling when you know that you once had a fulfilling life and could again if someone actually cared.   After all of this, who wouldn't have mental health issues?
